# 1 — Splunk Basics (5%)

---

## 1.1 Machine data

**Machine data** is any data generated by machines, systems or devices. It's produced automatically, in large volumes, and it's hard for humans to read raw.

Six examples from the course: **server logs, network logs, sensor data, application logs, security data, IoT data.**

> [!TIP]
> **Exam tell**
> "Logs, metrics, events produced automatically by systems" → machine data. Splunk handles **structured and unstructured** data.

## 1.2 What Splunk is — the 5 main functions

Splunk collects, **indexes**, searches, analyzes and visualizes machine data in real time ("a search engine for machine data").

| Function | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Index Data** | Ingest → break into **events** → parse fields → store in an **index** |
| **Search & Investigate** | Query with **SPL** (Search Processing Language) |
| **Add Knowledge** | Fields, **tags**, event types, **lookups**: context added to the data |
| **Monitor & Alert** | Watch conditions, trigger **alerts** and actions |
| **Report & Analyze** | **Reports, dashboards**, visualizations |

Memory hook: **I-S-A-M-R → "I Search And Monitor Reports."**

## 1.3 Splunk components

Pipeline: **Forwarder → Indexer → Search Head**

| Component | Job | Exam tells |
|---|---|---|
| **Forwarder** | Runs on the **source machine**, collects data and **forwards** it to indexers | "installed on the server that generates logs" |
| ↳ **Universal Forwarder (UF)** | Lightweight agent; collects and sends; **does not parse** | "lightweight", "minimal resources", "recommended way to send data" |
| ↳ **Heavy Forwarder (HF)** | **Full Splunk Enterprise instance**; can parse, filter, route, change data **before** forwarding | "filter/mask/route before indexing" |
| **Indexer** | Receives data, **parses, timestamps, stores** it in indexes; searches its own data. Uses time-based **buckets** | "stores", "processes", "timestamps", "buckets" |
| **Search Head** | The **web UI** where users search; sends the search to indexers and merges results; dashboards, reports, alerts | "where users write searches", "distributes searches" |

> [!NOTE]
> **Larger deployments add a **deployment server** (pushes configs to forwarders) and a **monitoring console** (health). Know they exist; they're barely tested on SPLK-1001.**

**Index-time phases (in order):** **Input** (read the source) → **Parsing** (break into events, timestamps, metadata) → **Indexing** (write to disk). License usage is metered at indexing.

## 1.4 Uses of Splunk

**IT operations** (monitoring, troubleshooting, capacity planning) · **Security & compliance** (detect, investigate, forensics, audit reporting) · **Business analytics** (customer behavior, campaigns) · **IoT**.

Security use-case pattern from the course: *detect → correlate logs across systems → find root cause (phishing → compromised account → exfiltration to a C2 server) → contain (disable the account, block the IP).*

## 1.5 Apps and add-ons

| | **App** | **Add-on** |
|---|---|---|
| What | A packaged **workspace/UI**: dashboards, reports, knowledge objects for a use case | A **reusable component**: data inputs, parsing, field extractions for a specific source |
| Has a UI? | Usually yes | Usually **no** |
| Example | Search & Reporting, Enterprise Security | Splunk Add-on for Windows / Cisco ASA |

- **Default app = Search & Reporting** (where you do almost everything).
- Apps live under `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/<app name>` (Windows: `C:\Program Files\Splunk\etc\apps\...`). An app is a **collection of configuration files**.
- Get apps from **Splunkbase** or from inside Splunk Web (*Find More Apps*). Most are free; premium apps (Enterprise Security, ITSI) need a license.
- **Splunk Built** = made by Splunk. **Splunk Certified** = third-party app that Splunk has **reviewed/validated**.

> [!WARNING]
> **⚠️ Common mix-up**
> Some study material says apps with the *Splunk Certified* logo "are made by Splunk". That's wrong. **Splunk Built = made by Splunk; Splunk Certified = checked by Splunk.**

## 1.6 Deployment types

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Standalone** | **One instance does everything**: input, indexing, search, UI. Labs and small environments |
| **Distributed** | **Multiple instances, each with a role** (forwarders, indexers, search heads); scales |
| **Cloud** | Like distributed, but **hosted and managed by a third party** (Splunk Cloud, on AWS/Azure) |

## 1.7 Navigation, users, roles

- **Splunk Web = browser, port 8000.** Other ports: **8089** management (splunkd), **9997** forwarder → indexer receiving, **514** syslog.
- **Home app / launcher** → app panel → **Splunk bar** (top: Apps, Settings, Activity → *Jobs*, *Triggered Alerts*, Messages, Help, Find).
- **3 main roles:**
  - **User**: search, create *private* knowledge objects.
  - **Power**: User + **share** knowledge objects, **create alerts / scheduled searches**.
  - **Admin**: everything (users, data inputs, config).
- **Account settings:** full name, email, password. **Preferences:** **time zone** (so timestamps line up with you; critical when correlating events), default app, SPL editor (themes, line numbers, autocomplete).

## 1.8 Getting data in (lightly tested)

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Upload** | A local file, indexed **once** |
| **Monitor** | Files & directories (continuous), TCP/UDP ports, HTTP Event Collector, scripts, Windows event logs |
| **Forward** | Receive data from **forwarders** (receiving port 9997) |

- End users **usually don't add data**. IT/DevOps or admins do.
- When data is added, you choose the **sourcetype** (how to parse) and the **index** (where to store).

## ⏱️ 60-second self-check

1. Name the 5 main functions of Splunk.
2. Which component parses, timestamps and stores data? Which one is the UI?
3. Universal vs heavy forwarder: which can filter before forwarding?
4. App vs add-on?
5. Splunk Web port? Forwarder receiving port?
6. The 3 deployment types? The 3 main roles, and which one can create alerts?
7. Why set your time zone?

<details><summary>Answers</summary>

1. Index Data · Search & Investigate · Add Knowledge · Monitor & Alert · Report & Analyze
2. Indexer; Search Head
3. Heavy forwarder (a full Splunk instance). The UF only collects and sends.
4. App = workspace/UI for a use case; add-on = input/parsing component, usually no UI
5. 8000; 9997
6. Standalone, Distributed, Cloud · User, Power, Admin. Power (and Admin) can create alerts.
7. So timestamps match your local time when you investigate and correlate events

</details>
